Here, we can see that Option 2 satisfy the logic.

Hence, the correct answer is** " Mountain: K2 "**.

questions.question:
In the question two statements are given, followed by two conclusions, I and II. You have to consider the statements to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions, if any, follows from the given statements.

**Statement** **I:** All napkins are towels

**Statement** **II:** All rags are napkins

**Conclusion** **I:** Some towels are rags

**Conclusion** **II:** All rags are towels

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor conclusion II follows

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ed0be213bb7d591720e35cda30671817b870a706e97a4a572209adcf610a3338.png] 

**Conclusion I:** Some towels are rags → True (As All napkins are towels and All rags are napkins)

**Conclusion II: **All rags are towels → True (As All napkins are towels and All rags are napkins)

Hence, the correct answer is **" Both conclusions I and II follow "**.

questions.question: In the following question, four groups of three numbers are given. In each group the second and third number are related to the first number by a Logic/Rule/Relation. Three are similar on basis of same Logic/Rule/Relation. Select the odd one out from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Second Number = (First Number + 3).**

**Third Number = (Second Number + 3).**

Let's check each option as per the logic,

1)** (31, 34, 37)**

→ 34 = (31 + 3)

→ 37 = (34 + 3)

2) **(43, 45, 48) **

→ 45 ≠ (43 + 3) → Doesn't satisfy the logic.

→ 48 = (45 + 3)

3) **(39, 42, 45)**

→ 42 = (39 + 3)

→ 45 = (42 + 3)

4) **(7, 10, 13)**

→ 10 = (7 + 3)

→ 13 = (10 + 3)

Here, we can see that only Option 2 doesn't satisfy the logic.

Hence, the correct answer is **" (43, 45, 48) "**.

questions.question: Which type of institution is the Finance Commission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitutional institution.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted as a constitutional body under "Article 280".
 
• It is constituted by the President of India. The Finance Commission in India is constituted under the Finance Commission Act 1951.
 
• It is a quasi-judicial institution and has a term of 5 years.
 
• The central government appointed N.K. Singh, a former member of the Planning Commission, as the chairman of the 15th Finance Commission on 27 November 2017.
 
• The Finance Commission sets the rules for grant money to the states from the Center.
 
• In Article 243 (I) and 243 (Y) of the Constitution of India, the State Finance Commissions are constituted every five years according to the constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first was the Finance Commission chaired by K. C. Niyogi (1952–1957).
 
• 13th Finance Commission headed by Dr. Vijay L. Kelkar (2010–2015).
 
• The 14th Finance Commission was headed by the former Governor of Reserve Bank of India Mr. Y.V. Reddy did.​
